Parse LOBSTER file and archive names

Source: R/files.R
lobster_file_info.Rd

LOBSTER names its files {ticker}_{date}_{start}_{end}_{type}_{levels}.csv, where start and end are the requested time window in milliseconds after midnight and type is message or orderbook. Monthly or daily archives are named {ticker}_{first date}_{last date}_{levels}.7z. This function extracts these fields from file names or full paths.

Usage

lobster_file_info(path)

Arguments

path

character Paths or file names. Compressed CSV files (.csv.gz, .csv.bz2, .csv.xz) and .parquet files that keep the LOBSTER name are recognised as well.

Value

A data.frame with one row per path and columns path, file ("message", "orderbook" or "archive", NA if the name does not follow the LOBSTER convention), ticker, date (first trading day), last_date (last trading day; equal to date for message and order book files), window_start and window_end (requested window in seconds after midnight; NA for archives) and levels.

Details

The time window in a file name is the window that was requested from LOBSTER. It does not mark the trading session: files often contain messages from long before the open to long after the close.

Examples

lobster_file_info(c(
  "SPY_2024-03-20_34200000_57600000_message_10.csv",
  "data/SPY_2024-03-20_34200000_57600000_orderbook_10.csv",
  "SPY_2024-02-27_2024-03-26_50.7z",
  "notes.txt"
))
#>                                                     path      file ticker
#> 1        SPY_2024-03-20_34200000_57600000_message_10.csv   message    SPY
#> 2 data/SPY_2024-03-20_34200000_57600000_orderbook_10.csv orderbook    SPY
#> 3                        SPY_2024-02-27_2024-03-26_50.7z   archive    SPY
#> 4                                              notes.txt      <NA>   <NA>
#>         date  last_date window_start window_end levels
#> 1 2024-03-20 2024-03-20        34200      57600     10
#> 2 2024-03-20 2024-03-20        34200      57600     10
#> 3 2024-02-27 2024-03-26           NA         NA     50
#> 4       <NA>       <NA>           NA         NA     NA
